steps.title: Define the attribute schema
steps.what: Material, fit, color and use case become a Pydantic schema; limits and 9 banned claims are read from the brand-voice SKILL.md.
steps.code:
class Enrichment(BaseModel):
    title: str; description: str
    material: str
    fit: Literal['relaxed','slim','regular','oversized','tapered','one size','unknown']
    color: str          # one of the store's swatches
    use_case: list[str]
steps.output:
fields: sku, title, description, material, fit, color, use_case, search_keywords
fit_values: relaxed, slim, regular, oversized, tapered, one size, unknown
color_facet: black, charcoal, heather grey, cream, navy, sky blue, forest green, olive, burgundy, red, rust, mustard, sand, pink
limits_from_skill: {'title_max_chars': 70, 'description_min_words': 25, 'description_max_words': 70}
banned_from_skill: eco-friendly, sustainable, best, guaranteed, waterproof, antibacterial, hypoallergenic, miracle, cures

story.situation: An apparel store with 4,000 SKUs from 30 suppliers. Titles look like 'TEE-101 NVY', and material, fit and color filters are mostly empty, so search misses products and shoppers return items that were not what they expected.
story.constraints: Copy must not make claims the brand can't back (waterproof, eco-friendly, antibacterial). Colors must use the store's swatch list or the filters break. A merchandiser signs off before anything goes live. The job runs overnight, so the Batch API halves the cost.
story.replay: Reuse: photo + spec sheet -> schema -> batch -> deterministic checks -> human sample is the same shape for any listing job (real estate, auto parts, marketplaces). Next time: put the banned-claims list in the checker and the skill from day one, and A/B test the new copy on search click-through before rolling out to all SKUs.

metrics.search_clicks: needs a live A/B test; not measurable offline
